rationale: bugs_open/071 gap 3, the residual half. validate_page_content has three outcomes and only two recorders: writeValidationFailureLog fires only on !valid (validate_page_content.go:409/:426) and deliberately excludes warnings; writeLinkRepairLog fires on the success path only when len(repairs)>0 (:449/:457). A VALID build whose warnings produced no repair — short_content, stat_audit_unavailable, any phantom_link when the page index was unavailable or repair_internal_links is off — therefore writes NOTHING durable: the issue list survives only in the action's return map -> collected_data, which database-cleanup prunes at ~24h, and one pod log line carrying the count but not the detail. This is exactly the mechanism 071 was filed about (the gate detects, then the finding evaporates), surviving in a narrowed form after the repair work landed. The fix adds the third member of the existing recorder family: writeValidationWarningLog, called on the success path, gated on >=1 SURVIVING warning, writing one agent_error_log row per build under a NEW error_code CONTENT_VALIDATION_WARNING_DETAIL (the file's own :639-style invariant: existing queries on the two sibling codes must keep returning exactly what they returned). Dedupe: a link warning whose href the repair pass acted on is excluded — it is already durably recorded in the repair row's context.repairs — via repairsByHref, a helper extracted from annotateLinkRepairs so the annotator and the filter cannot drift. The filter is a pure function (survivingWarnings) because a mocked best-effort writer cannot assert the negative; the no-write case is pinned on the filter's empty return, and the exclusion is mutation-proven (ok && false mutant fails 3 tests). Volume bounded: one row per valid build carrying an unrepaired warning; 661 pages deployed fleet-wide in 7 days is the ~94/day upper bound, and the sibling repair code runs ~15 rows/day without complaint.

The write/no-write negative is pinned on the pure filter because agenterrors.Write is best-effort and swallows an unexpected exec.
